messages:
lina: Heads-up — I hit a pretty reproducible OOM when the shard allocator does a tiny-page split under bursty offload. Repro steps attached below.

devon: ugh, that's the split path we barely exercised in perf tests. can you paste the minimal repro?

lina: Yep. gist: we run 64 concurrent tiny allocations (~8KB) then trigger host-staging eviction; after ~2s the allocator tries to split a tiny slab and ends up with freed metadata but not updating the residency map quickly enough. log: ```
[2024-11-02T12:03:21Z] evictor: offload request queued tenant=42 pages=128
[2024-11-02T12:03:21Z] allocator: split tiny-slab id=0x7fa3 status=started
[2024-11-02T12:03:21Z] gfx: register-page failed: ENOMEM
```

patrick: that sounds like an ordering bug: free metadata (slab header) races with gfx register / hostmap update. we may be dropping a refcount before the hostpage pin completes.

lina: my local trace shows the refcount decrement happens on the compaction path, but compaction yields to the eviction worker which immediately tries to reuse the same slab descriptor.

devon: do we have an invariant that slab descriptors are only recycled after hostmap ack? if not, we should add one.

patrick: we currently rely on a handshake: compaction -> mark freed -> notify residency collector -> free-to-reuse. but the residency collector is on a background timer (100ms) which is too long under burst.

sara: could we change to an immediate async ack on critical paths? or have the eviction worker back off if the descriptor is in-flight?

lina: two proposed fixes I sketched: 1) fast-path: bump a 'recycle hold' ref on split until hostmap register returns; 2) tighten the invariant: don't allow reuse until the residency collector confirms. option 1 is less invasive.

patrick: option 1 seems safest to land fast. add a short-lived token on the descriptor so reuse checks fail until cleared. we should measure overhead.

devon: agree. add a metric like `allocator.descriptor_inflight` and a debug counter that increments on fast-path hold. also add a smoke test that floods tiny allocations + eviction for 10s.

ci-bot: note: created ticket RW-ops#1846 for the fix and test.

lina: I'll draft a PR for the token pattern. rough patch outline: ```c
// on split start
desc->inflight_hold = true;
// after hostmap register callback
desc->inflight_hold = false;
// reuse path checks: if (desc->inflight_hold) return EBUSY;
```

patrick: careful about memory ordering, use an atomic with acquire/release. also consider the case where register callback never comes (timeout). add a fallback timer to clear hold and emit telemetry.

devon: can we avoid a timeout by making hostmap register synchronous on the split fast-path? might hurt tail latency. prefer async + timeout.

lina: agreed. I'll implement atomic hold + 500ms fallback and the new metric. if fallback hits we'll log with `evictor.debug` and increment `allocator.hold_timeouts`.

sara: also add a canary to auto-run on every commit in CI (flaky test tolerated) so we catch regressions.

lina: plan posted in RW-ops#1846. I'll send a short PR and ping for review. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

devon: thanks — want me to pair on the smoke test harness?

lina: please, that would speed it up. @devon

patrick: after the quick fix lands we should follow up with a postmortem-style doc describing why the residency collector timer existed and whether we should change the collector design long-term (i.e., event-driven).

lina: noted. I'll add a follow-up card for an event-driven residency collector RFC.
